title: Mark Chapman Drops NZ Central Contract to Chase Big Bash League Opportunity
excerpt: The New Zealand batter will play the white-ball series against India in November before heading to Australia for the BBL, while fast bowler Matt Fisher takes his spot on the full-time contract list.
body:
• New Zealand batter Mark Chapman has shifted to a casual contract with NZC to pursue a Big Bash League deal in Australia this December.
  • Chapman remains available for the white-ball series against India in November before heading to the BBL.
  • Fast bowler Matt Fisher has been elevated to the full-time central contract list, bolstering New Zealand's pace depth for upcoming Test series against India, Australia and Sri Lanka.
  • Chapman joins Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert on casual contracts that prioritise T20 franchise cricket over domestic matches.

New Zealand batter Mark Chapman has given up his full-time central contract to pursue a stint in the Australian Big Bash League, New Zealand Cricket announced on Monday.

The left-hander will shift to a casual playing agreement for the 2026-27 season, joining four other New Zealand internationals — Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert — who hold similar deals allowing them to play T20 franchise cricket abroad during the home summer.

India Series Commitment Remains

Chapman was quick to reassure fans that his commitment to international cricket has not wavered. He will be available for the upcoming white-ball series against India in November before departing for Australia. His BBL club has not yet been confirmed.

"I'm thankful to New Zealand Cricket for their support now and throughout my career. The upcoming India series is one all us players are really excited for, and I'm committed wholeheartedly to performing in that series."

— Mark Chapman, New Zealand batter

The 32-year-old, who was born in Hong Kong and represented the territory before qualifying for New Zealand, has played 113 T20 internationals and scored over 2,000 runs in the format. He has never played a Test for New Zealand despite being called into the squad during the 2024 tour of India, and earlier this year he asked not to be considered for Test selection when NZC drew up its initial contract list.

Fisher Gets Full-Time Deal

Chapman's move off the main list has opened a spot for Northern Districts fast bowler Matt Fisher, who now holds his first-ever central contract. Fisher, who has featured across all three formats, recently took career-best ODI figures of 3-40 against the West Indies to help seal just the second ODI series win in the Caribbean for New Zealand.

NZC selection manager Gavin Larsen said the addition was made with squad depth in mind. "With the heavy schedule of cricket coming up, notably the Test matches against India, Australia, and Sri Lanka, we know we'll need good depth in our fast-bowling stocks to give the Black Caps the best chance of success," Larsen said. "Matt is someone able to bowl that express pace which is extremely valuable to the balance of any side."

The T20 Franchise Tug-of-War

Chapman's decision reflects a growing trend across world cricket. Players are increasingly weighing the financial rewards of T20 franchise leagues against the demands of year-round international commitments. New Zealand has been particularly affected — Trent Boult, one of the finest T20 bowlers in the game, has played just two matches at home since 2022 due to commitments with Mumbai Indians and its affiliate franchises.

The BBL runs concurrently with New Zealand's Test tour of Australia later this summer. Since Chapman has effectively ruled himself out of red-ball cricket, the scheduling conflict does not apply to him, but the broader pattern of white-ball specialists choosing franchise money over domestic cricket continues to reshape squad planning for every cricket board.

What's Next

Chapman is expected to feature in the T20I and ODI series against India starting in November. NZC's chief high performance officer Daryl Gibson said Chapman's shift creates opportunity further down the system, freeing up a contract spot at Northern Districts for another developing player. Fisher, who has played one Test, three ODIs and one T20I, will look to cement his place in the pace rotation as New Zealand prepares for a packed home summer.
